transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me today. Am I sitting in the right spot? Okay, good. 

Um... well, I guess what brings me in is... it's a little embarrassing to admit at my age, and I really don't want to make a big fuss out of it, but... I just have this trouble sitting still. It's like I feel like I've got this little motor humming right under my skin whenever I'm supposed to just stay put. Like during the morning staff meetings at the building I clean, or, you know, church event briefings. 

I really try my best to be polite and just listen, I promise I do, but I always end up shifting around in my chair a lot. Or I'll just stand in the back of the room, or find some excuse to go check the cleaning supplies just so I can move around a bit. I hope that makes sense? I just don't want people thinking I'm being rude or not paying attention, you know? Is that... is that the sort of thing I should be bringing up here?
Can you recall if this restlessness or need to move started when you were a child, or did it begin more recently?

Oh, gosh... well, I suppose it's been there for a very long time. Since I was a kid, really. I wasn't a bad kid, I promise! I just... I guess I had a bit too much energy. 

I remember back in grade school, I'd get into a little bit of trouble sometimes because I'd, well, I'd pop out of my seat without meaning to. Or I'd accidentally talk over the teacher. I really didn't mean any disrespect at all, I'd just get so eager to start things that I'd rush ahead before they even finished giving the directions. 

My mother, bless her, she used to always say I acted like I was wound just a little too tight, even as a young boy. 

Does that help answer your question, Doctor? I hope I'm explaining it right. I really wasn't trying to be a nuisance back then, I just... couldn't seem to help it. Is that the kind of thing you needed to know?
Can you tell me if you also find it hard to stay focused or tend to get easily distracted, especially when you're trying to complete tasks or listen to someone for a while?

Oh, um... well, no, not really. I mean, I'm pretty good at getting my work done. I take a lot of pride in keeping the building nice and clean, you know? 

I suppose sometimes my mind might wander just a tiny bit if someone is talking for a very, very long time, but I think that happens to everyone, right? I always make sure to nod and smile so they know I'm listening. I really try my best to be a good listener. 

And as for my tasks, I just kind of keep moving from one thing to the next. Sometimes I might start sweeping and then notice a smudge on the glass and go clean that, but it all gets done by the end of the shift! I'm a very hard worker, I promise. 

So, no, I wouldn't say I have trouble focusing. Does that make sense? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of answers.

Sometimes people feel like they act on impulse or say things without really thinking them through. Do you ever find yourself doing that, like maybe interrupting others or making quick decisions without considering the consequences?

Oh, gosh... well, I wouldn't say I make bad decisions or do anything reckless. I'm very responsible, I promise! But... um... I suppose sometimes with the talking part... I might do that just a little bit. 

Like, when my supervisor at the building, or maybe one of the church staff is giving me instructions for the day... I just want to show them I'm on top of it and ready to help, you know? So I'll sort of... jump in. I end up saying what I think they're going to tell me to do before they even finish their sentence. 

And... well, sometimes I guess I get it wrong, and they have to stop and correct me. It's awfully embarrassing when that happens. I always apologize right away! I really don't mean to interrupt them or be disrespectful, I just get a little too eager to get to work, I think. 

I hope that's not too terrible? I really do try to be polite. Does that answer what you were asking, Doctor?
Do you find yourself feeling restless or interrupting others in situations outside of work or church, like at home with family or in social gatherings?

Oh, well... I suppose it's not just at work or church. But I really do try to keep it under control! My wife and I, we like to go fishing sometimes, or we'll go down to the community center for bingo night. Just nice, quiet things, you know? 

But... well, even when I'm supposed to be relaxing and just enjoying the quiet, I guess I still get a little fidgety. Like at bingo, I might be tapping my foot or messing around with the dauber or my pencil, and I don't even realize I'm doing it. Or when we're fishing, I'll start reorganizing my tackle box for the third time or maybe I'll start talking just a little too loud when the fish aren't biting. 

My wife will give me that look, and I know I need to settle down. It's just... it gets a bit hard for me to just sit still and be quiet, even when I really want to. I hope that doesn't make me sound like a bother to be around. I'm just trying to be honest with you. Is that the kind of thing you were wondering about?
Can you tell me if you often feel restless or have trouble staying still in other situations, like when you're alone at home or trying to rest in bed at night?

Oh, um... well, yes, I suppose I do keep pretty busy. But it's a good thing, right? It means things get done! 

Like, when I'm on my shift at the building, I just sort of... keep moving. I'll go right from mopping the floors to checking the trash cans, and then maybe straightening up the chairs in the lobby, all without really taking a break. I just like to make sure everything looks nice for everyone. 

And, um, even when I get home... I know I should probably just sit down and rest after a long day of work, but I usually end up out in the garage. I'll just start puttering around, you know? Maybe I'll re-sort my tools or tinker with something that doesn't really need fixing. I just... I feel better when I'm doing something. Sitting on the couch just feels a little too... quiet, I guess. 

I hope that's okay? I mean, keeping active is supposed to be good for you at my age, isn't it? I just want to make sure I'm not doing anything wrong.
Do you ever find it hard to pay attention or stay focused when you’re not at work or in structured settings, like when you’re reading, watching TV, or having a conversation at home?

Oh, gosh, no, I don't think I have trouble with that. I really do try my best to be a good listener, I promise! 

If my wife is telling me about her day, I make sure to hear every word. I mean... I might be sorting the mail or maybe tinkering with a loose hinge on the cabinet while she's talking, but I'm definitely paying attention to her! And with TV... well, I follow the shows just fine. I might get up to wipe down the kitchen counters during the commercials, or fold some laundry, but I never lose track of the story. 

I don't read a whole lot of big books, to be honest, but I can read the paper or a magazine without any problem. I always want to make sure I'm giving people my full attention because it's just the polite thing to do, right? I hope that's a good thing. I just haven't really noticed any issues with losing focus like that... does that make sense, Doctor?

Can you think of a time when you were trying to focus on something that wasn't work or a structured activity—maybe a hobby, a conversation, or relaxing at home—where you found it hard to pay attention or keep your mind from wandering, even if you didn’t notice it at the time?

Well, um... I really can't think of anything like that. I mean, I try very hard to be present, you know? If my wife and I are sitting on the porch or if a neighbor stops by to chat, I'm right there with them. 

I guess... well, maybe sometimes I'll be thinking about the gutters needing cleaning or whether I put the right fertilizer on the lawn while we're talking, but I'm still listening! I always nod and smile and make sure they know I'm engaged. I would hate for anyone to think I was ignoring them, that would just be awful. 

And when I'm relaxing... well, like I said before, my kind of relaxing is usually just keeping my hands busy. But my mind doesn't really wander off to where I forget what I'm doing. I just like to stay productive, that's all. I really hope that's normal... I mean, it's not a bad thing to be a little proactive around the house, is it? I just don't think I have that problem with my mind wandering away from things.
Can you tell me if there have been times when you’ve struggled to stay focused on something you were doing for enjoyment, like a hobby or a conversation, even if it wasn’t work-related?

Oh, um... I know you sort of just asked about that, and I really want to give you a good answer, I do! But honestly... no, I don't think I struggle with that. 

Like, if I'm doing something I enjoy, say, um, working on a little woodworking project out in the garage... I'm right there doing it. I mean, sure, I might have the radio on, and I might bounce between sanding one piece and measuring another just to keep things moving, but I wouldn't call it a struggle to stay focused. I'm just enjoying myself! And with conversations, like I said, I really pride myself on being polite and paying attention to folks. 

I really hope I'm not being difficult or answering this wrong, Doctor. I just want to be completely honest with you so I don't waste your time. Is it okay that I don't really have that problem?
Can you tell me if you often feel a need to be constantly moving or feel restless, even when you’re not trying to focus on a task or be in a quiet situation?

Well, um... I wouldn't really use the word "restless," if that's okay. I just like to stay busy! I hope that's alright to say. I've always just thought of myself as a hard worker. 

Like at work—I'm a building cleaner, you know—and on my shifts I just kind of keep moving. I'll go right from mopping the floors to checking the trash cans, and then maybe straightening up the chairs in the breakroom, all without really stopping. But that just makes me a good employee, right? I always want to make sure I'm doing a thorough job. 

And I guess... well, even when I get home, I don't really just sit down after work. I'll usually head straight out and start puttering around in the garage, maybe re-sorting my tools or fixing something up. I just feel better when I'm doing something useful, you know? I mean, it's better to be active than lazy, don't you think? I really hope I'm answering your question right... I just like to keep on my feet!
Can you tell me if these feelings of needing to move or being overly active have ever caused you any real problems—like trouble with your job, relationships, or other parts of your life?

Oh, um... well, I guess... maybe a little bit? I mean, I try so hard to be a good employee, I really do. I always want to do my best for them. 

But, um... lately, there have been a few... well, I guess you could call them complaints. Or just corrections, really! It's just that because I'm always moving so fast and trying to get things done, sometimes I... well, I might miss a small part of the instructions they give me. And then during room turnovers, or when we're making supply decisions, I guess I can get a little ahead of myself and it creates some... friction with the rest of the team. 

I hate that, I really do. I never want to be a bother or make anyone's job harder. It actually got to the point where my supervisor... well, he kind of pushed me toward the employee assistance program. He was very nice about it, of course, but... it made me feel just awful, honestly. I just want to do a good job. Is it okay that I'm admitting this? I really hope it doesn't make me sound like a bad worker... I just get a little too eager to keep moving, I think.
Doctor: Can you tell me if you often feel worried or on edge, even when there isn’t anything specific that’s bothering you?

Oh, um... worried? No, I don't think so. I really don't want to come across as a nervous person, because I don't think I am! 

I mean, I like to be prepared and do things right, like I said, but I wouldn't say I sit around feeling on edge or anxious for no reason. If I have a lot to do, sure, I want to get it done, but I don't feel... scared or worried about it. I just like to stay busy and keep things moving. 

I hope that's the right kind of answer. I just don't want to make things up or sound like I'm complaining about things that aren't there. Does that make sense, Doctor? I really try to just keep a positive attitude about things.
Have you ever found yourself stuck on certain thoughts or ideas, or felt like you had to do things a certain way to make things feel 'just right'?

Oh, um... stuck on thoughts? No, I don't think so. I really hope it's okay to say no to that! I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers. 

I mean, I like things to look nice and clean at work, of course, but I don't get... well, I don't get hung up on things having to be exactly perfect or done in one specific order. If my supervisor needs me to drop what I'm doing and go handle a spill somewhere else, I just jump right to it! I'm pretty flexible that way. I don't feel like things have to be exactly 'just right' before I can move on, I just try to do the best I can with whatever they ask me to do. 

Is that... does that answer what you were asking, Doctor? I really just want to be as helpful as I can.

I really hope I'm not being difficult or answering this wrong, Doctor. I just want to be completely honest with you so I don't waste your time. Is it okay that I don't really have that problem?

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences symptoms of hyperactivity or restlessness in a variety of settings, which is a key feature of ADHD (F90.0).
doctor.question: Can you tell me if you often feel a need to be constantly moving or feel restless, even when you’re not trying to focus on a task or be in a quiet situation?

target_item.name: Constant_Activity
target_item.manifestation: On my shifts I go from mopping to checking trash to straightening chairs without really stopping, and even at home I’ll start puttering in the garage or re-sorting tools instead of sitting down after work.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if I feel a constant need to be moving or feel restless, even when not focusing on a task, which aligns with being 'on the go' or acting as if 'driven by a motor' (Constant_Activity).

patient.answer:
Well, um... I wouldn't really use the word "restless," if that's okay. I just like to stay busy! I hope that's alright to say. I've always just thought of myself as a hard worker. 

Like at work—I'm a building cleaner, you know—and on my shifts I just kind of keep moving. I'll go right from mopping the floors to checking the trash cans, and then maybe straightening up the chairs in the breakroom, all without really stopping. But that just makes me a good employee, right? I always want to make sure I'm doing a thorough job. 

And I guess... well, even when I get home, I don't really just sit down after work. I'll usually head straight out and start puttering around in the garage, maybe re-sorting my tools or fixing something up. I just feel better when I'm doing something useful, you know? I mean, it's better to be active than lazy, don't you think? I really hope I'm answering your question right... I just like to keep on my feet!

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences significant impairment in social, occupational, or other important areas of functioning due to their symptoms, which would help distinguish between F90.0 (ADHD predominantly inattentive type) and other candidates like F42.2 (OCD), F43.10 (PTSD), or F44.7 (Dissociative disorder).
doctor.question: Can you tell me if these feelings of needing to move or being overly active have ever caused you any real problems—like trouble with your job, relationships, or other parts of your life?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: At work it has started causing complaints and corrections because I miss parts of instructions and create friction during room turnovers and supply decisions, to the point my supervisor pushed me toward the employee assistance program.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the symptoms (needing to move/being overly active) have caused any real problems, such as trouble with job, relationships, or other parts of life, which maps directly to functional impairment.

patient.answer:
Oh, um... well, I guess... maybe a little bit? I mean, I try so hard to be a good employee, I really do. I always want to do my best for them. 

But, um... lately, there have been a few... well, I guess you could call them complaints. Or just corrections, really! It's just that because I'm always moving so fast and trying to get things done, sometimes I... well, I might miss a small part of the instructions they give me. And then during room turnovers, or when we're making supply decisions, I guess I can get a little ahead of myself and it creates some... friction with the rest of the team. 

I hate that, I really do. I never want to be a bother or make anyone's job harder. It actually got to the point where my supervisor... well, he kind of pushed me toward the employee assistance program. He was very nice about it, of course, but... it made me feel just awful, honestly. I just want to do a good job. Is it okay that I'm admitting this? I really hope it doesn't make me sound like a bad worker... I just get a little too eager to keep moving, I think.

inference.note: This turn provided more insight into the patient's symptoms causing functional impairment at work, which supports ruling out F44.7 (Dissociative amnesia) as there is no evidence of memory loss or dissociation. The remaining candidates (F90.0 - ADHD, F42.2 - OCD, F43.10 - Generalized Anxiety Disorder) still fit based on the patient's restlessness, difficulty staying still, and some impulsivity, though no clear obsessions, compulsions, or anxiety symptoms were reported.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences symptoms of anxiety that could support a diagnosis of F43.10 (Generalized Anxiety Disorder).
doctor.question: Doctor: Can you tell me if you often feel worried or on edge, even when there isn’t anything specific that’s bothering you?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about feeling worried or on edge (symptoms of generalized anxiety), which is not covered by any of the ADHD-hyperactive/impulsive symptom profiles provided.

patient.answer:
Oh, um... worried? No, I don't think so. I really don't want to come across as a nervous person, because I don't think I am! 

I mean, I like to be prepared and do things right, like I said, but I wouldn't say I sit around feeling on edge or anxious for no reason. If I have a lot to do, sure, I want to get it done, but I don't feel... scared or worried about it. I just like to stay busy and keep things moving. 

I hope that's the right kind of answer. I just don't want to make things up or sound like I'm complaining about things that aren't there. Does that make sense, Doctor? I really try to just keep a positive attitude about things.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences symptoms of obsessive thoughts or compulsive behaviors that may indicate OCD (F42.2).
doctor.question: Have you ever found yourself stuck on certain thoughts or ideas, or felt like you had to do things a certain way to make things feel 'just right'?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about obsessive thoughts or compulsive behaviors (OCD symptoms) like needing things to be 'just right', which is not covered in my symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Oh, um... stuck on thoughts? No, I don't think so. I really hope it's okay to say no to that! I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers. 

I mean, I like things to look nice and clean at work, of course, but I don't get... well, I don't get hung up on things having to be exactly perfect or done in one specific order. If my supervisor needs me to drop what I'm doing and go handle a spill somewhere else, I just jump right to it! I'm pretty flexible that way. I don't feel like things have to be exactly 'just right' before I can move on, I just try to do the best I can with whatever they ask me to do. 

Is that... does that answer what you were asking, Doctor? I really just want to be as helpful as I can.

inference.note: The patient's symptoms of restlessness, difficulty staying still, and impulsive behavior (e.g., interrupting others) began in childhood and persist into adulthood. There is no evidence of compulsive thoughts or behaviors (ruling out F42.2) and no indication of prolonged stress or trauma (ruling out F43.10). Symptoms are consistent with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, predominantly hyperactive/impulsive presentation.
